contexts.title: A narrower policy interval can be more confidently wrong

findings: Complete 534-line chapter14 source read, with the entire added recovery section and physical pages102–109; original bootstrap study and all adverse cases remain verbatim.

Successful truthful recovery, known positive probabilities, independent customers and fixed policies are explicit. Invitations, missing terminal balances and selective completion do not satisfy the history-recovery requirement.

The mean/variance recovery identity, sequential telescoping and conditional cross-fit argument preserve their assumptions; pooled-score variance requires the stated deterministic L2 limit, not cross-fitting alone.

All67500 retained CSV rows across3500 scenario replications reaggregate into135 method-target groups. Independent-pilot precision is explicitly unequal-budget; the7000-record comparison matches realised collection resources.

The adverse cross-fit coverage remains94.4 percent rather than a95 percent guarantee. False routine weights retain substantial bias and confident positive decisions. No bank data, feasible recovery or operating prices are claimed.

Inherited source has no deletions. Five imported decimal transcriptions are corrected against retained records and listed in integration.json; two added genuine primary records and two original figures remain traceable.
scope: Complete current chapter14 source author reading and complete added-section rendered-text review; no fresh whole-book, visual or independent acceptance.
